claim: Breast, bladder, lung, neuroglioma, and prostate cancer cells treated with 6 Gy X-ray radiation and cultured for 72 hours showed an increase in lipid droplet (LD) number.
source: To verify whether LD content was affected by ionizing radiation treatment, H4 (neuroglioma), H460 (lung), MCF7 (breast), PC3 (prostate), and T24 (bladder) cancer cells were treated with 6 Gy X-ray and left in culture for 72 hours (hrs) in order to select only surviving and resistant cells. Treated and untreated cancer cells were stained with LD540 and imaged at the confocal microscope for the detection of LDs. As shown by z-projection confocal microscopy images, surviving cancer cells were characterized by a significant increase of LDs for all the aforementioned cell lines (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from confocal microscopy imaging showing increased LDs in all tested cell lines after 6 Gy radiation treatment, as shown in Figure 1A.

claim: H460 cells exhibited the highest relative LD ratio between treated and untreated cells among all tested cell lines.
source: Although the LD increase was a common feature observed in all cell lines, the relative LD ratio between treated and untreated cells showed little differences, with H460 exhibiting the highest amount (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data presented in Figure 1B comparing LD ratios across different cell lines.

claim: PLIN1 was upregulated in H460, MCF7, PC3, and T24 cells after 6 Gy radiation treatment.
source: Accordingly, we observed that, after 6 Gy radiation treatment, PLIN1 was upregulated in H460, MCF7, PC3, and T24
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data showing PLIN1 mRNA expression changes after radiation treatment.

claim: PLIN2 was downregulated in H460 cells after 6 Gy radiation treatment.
source: PLIN2 was downregulated in H460
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data showing PLIN2 mRNA expression changes after radiation treatment.

claim: PLIN3 showed increased mRNA expression in H4 and MCF7 cells after 6 Gy radiation treatment.
source: PLIN3 showed mRNA increased expression in H4 and MCF7
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data showing PLIN3 mRNA expression changes after radiation treatment.

claim: PLIN4 expression was increased in MCF7 and T24 cells after 6 Gy radiation treatment.
source: PLIN4 expression was incremented in MCF7 and T24
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data showing PLIN4 mRNA expression changes after radiation treatment.

claim: PLIN5 was downregulated in MCF7 cells after 6 Gy radiation treatment.
source: PLIN5 resulted downregulated in MCF7
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data showing PLIN5 mRNA expression changes after radiation treatment.

claim: PLIN5 was upregulated in PC3 and T24 cells after 6 Gy radiation treatment.
source: PLIN5 resulted downregulated in MCF7 and upregulated in PC3 and T24.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data showing PLIN5 mRNA expression changes after radiation treatment.

claim: Photon radiation produces reactive oxygen species (ROS) at the molecular level.
source: It is well known that photon radiation acts, at the molecular level, producing reactive oxygen species (ROS) (Schonberg, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Schonberg, 2015, indicating established scientific knowledge.

claim: Cytoplasmic ROS were significantly upregulated in H4, H460, MCF7, and PC3 cells after radiation treatment.
source: In this regard, we found that cytoplasmatic ROS, measured by means of fluorogenic CM-H2DCFDA probe, were significantly upregulated in H4, H460, MCF7, and PC3, while no differences were detected in T24, after radiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using CM-H2DCFDA probe measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No differences in ROS levels were detected in T24 cells after radiation treatment.
source: In this regard, we found that cytoplasmatic ROS, measured by means of fluorogenic CM-H2DCFDA probe, were significantly upregulated in H4, H460, MCF7, and PC3, while no differences were detected in T24, after radiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using CM-H2DCFDA probe measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H4, H460, and PC3 cells showed upregulated levels of SOD1, SOD2, and catalase, respectively, after radiation treatment.
source: Moreover, H4, H460, and PC3 showed upregulated levels of SOD1, SOD2, and catalase, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data from qPCR analysis.

claim: SOD2 mRNA was upregulated in T24 cells 72 hours after radiation treatment despite general ROS levels not being altered.
source: SOD2 mRNA was also upregulated in T24, despite the fact that general ROS levels were not altered 72 hrs after radiation treatment
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data from qPCR analysis combined with ROS measurements.

claim: SOD expression was downregulated in radiation-treated MCF7 cells.
source: while SOD expression was downregulated in radiation-treated MCF7. (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cancer cells need to tune their ROS scavenging systems to deal with ROS increase.
source: In order to deal with this ROS increase, cancer cells need to tune their ROS scavenging systems (Trachootham et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Trachootham et al., 2009, indicating established scientific knowledge.

claim: Lipid droplets contribute to the modulation of excessive oxidative stress.
source: and among all scavenging systems, LDs have been observed to contribute to the modulation of excessive oxidative stress (Welte, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Welte, 2015, indicating established scientific knowledge.

claim: Populations with higher LDs also exhibited higher levels of ROS in not-irradiated cancer cells.
source: Furthermore, by co-staining LDs and ROS in the heterogeneous not-irradiated cancer populations, we found that populations with higher LDs also exhibited higher levels of ROS (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from co-staining experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: LD content is directly correlated with ROS production in all tested cell lines.
source: Therefore, LD content, influencing cell survival, was directly correlated with ROS production in all cell lines.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the co-staining data showing correlation between LD and ROS levels.

claim: Ionizing radiation can selectively enrich the cancer cell population with cells having stem-like properties.
source: Previous works reported that ionizing radiation could selectively enrich the cancer cell population of cells with stem-like properties (Ghisolfi et al., 2012; Krause et al., 2017; Woodward et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple previous studies (Ghisolfi et al., 2012; Krause et al., 2017; Woodward et al., 2007).

claim: CD44 was upregulated in 6 Gy treated H4, H460, MCF7, and T24 cells.
source: In particular, we found that CD44 was upregulated in 6 Gy treated H4, H460, MCF7 and T24
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data of CSC marker expression.

claim: CD133 mRNA increased in H4 and H460 irradiated cells.
source: CD133 mRNA increased in H4 and H460-irradiated cells
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data of CSC marker expression.

claim: CD166 expression was upregulated in MCF7 and T24 cells after radiation treatment.
source: CD166 expression was upregulated in MCF7 and T24
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data of CSC marker expression.

claim: ALDH1 was increased in MCF7 cells after radiation treatment.
source: ALDH1 was incremented in MCF7.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data of CSC marker expression.

claim: PC3 radioresistant cells did not display significant increase in the expression of CSC markers.
source: On the contrary, PC3 RR cells did not display significant increase in the expression of such CSC markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: LDHigh cells retained the highest clonogenic potential compared to LDLow cells across all tested cell lines.
source: The surviving fractions (SFs), calculated for all cell lines at the different doses, showed that LDHigh cells retained the highest clonogenic potential and therefore they were the most radioresistant (Figure 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by clonogenic assay data shown in Figure 2 comparing survival fractions of LDHigh and LDLow populations.

claim: The LD amount present in the population is linked to a stronger cell capability to survive ionizing radiations, independently of the tissue of origin.
source: These results suggest that the LD amount present in the population is linked to a stronger cell capability to survive ionizing radiations, independently of the tissue of origin.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the clonogenic assay results showing consistent pattern across different cancer cell types.

claim: The Fenton reaction is one of the main cellular ROS sources, in which Fe2+ reacts with hydrogen peroxide to produce Fe3+ and highly reactive radicals such as the hydroxyl radical.
source: One of the main cellular ROS sources is the Fenton reaction, in which the Fe2+ reacts with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) to produce Fe3+ and highly reactive radicals, such as the hydroxyl radical (∙OH).
evidence: The claim represents established scientific knowledge about the Fenton reaction mechanism.

claim: Ferritin is the main intracellular iron storage protein.
source: Since the Ferritin is the main intracellular iron storage protein, we investigated the FTH1 role in radiation resistance.
evidence: The claim represents established scientific knowledge about ferritin function.

claim: FTH1 protein was upregulated in all resistant cell lines after 72 hours from 6 Gy exposure.
source: We found that FTH1 protein was upregulated in all resistant cell lines after 72 hrs from 6 Gy exposure, as reported in Figure 3A,B.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: H460 and MCF7 LDhigh subpopulations were characterized by an increase in the mRNA level of FTH1 compared to LDlow cells.
source: Moreover, H460 and MCF7, sorted on the basis of their LD content, were characterized by an increase in the mRNA level of FTH1 in the LDhigh subpopulation compared to the LDlow cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data shown in Figure 3C comparing FTH1 expression in sorted populations.

claim: FTH1 gene silencing caused a LD decrease in both H460 and MCF7 cell systems.
source: LD540 staining revealed that the FTH1 gene silencing caused a LD decrease in both cell systems.
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data showing reduced LD content in FTH1-silenced cells.

claim: FTH1 silencing in H460 and MCF7 cells resulted in downregulation of Transferrin Receptor 1 (TfR1) mRNA.
source: FTH1 silencing resulted in influencing cell ability to deal with free cytoplasmic iron, as demonstrated by the downregulation of Transferrin Receptor 1 (TfR1) mRNA and the upregulation of Ferroportin (FPN) mRNA, all involved in proper iron homeostasis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: FTH1 silencing in H460 and MCF7 cells resulted in upregulation of Ferroportin (FPN) mRNA.
source: FTH1 silencing resulted in influencing cell ability to deal with free cytoplasmic iron, as demonstrated by the downregulation of Transferrin Receptor 1 (TfR1) mRNA and the upregulation of Ferroportin (FPN) mRNA, all involved in proper iron homeostasis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The amount of FTH1 directly correlated with the number of LDs in FTH1 silenced H460 and MCF7 cells.
source: Interestingly, in FTH1 silenced H460 and MCF7, the amount of FTH1 directly correlated with the number of LDs (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3E,F comparing LD content in FTH1-silenced cells.

claim: H460 shFTH1 and MCF7 shFTH1 cells were characterized by a significant reduction of LDs.
source: In fact, H460 shFTH1 and MCFshFTH1 cells were characterized by a significant reduction of LDs.
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data showing reduced LD content in FTH1-silenced cells.

claim: Reduction of LDs in FTH1-silenced cells led to an evident increase in radiosensitivity.
source: This, in turn, led to an evident increase in the radiosensitivity, as demonstrated by the clonogenic assay results (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by clonogenic assay data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: LD content is dependent on FTH1 expression and linked to free cytoplasmic iron.
source: Summarizing, we show that LD content was dependent on the FTH1 expression and thus linked to the free cytoplasmic iron.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing correlation between FTH1 expression, LD content, and iron metabolism.

claim: When levels of the main protein responsible for iron storage decreased, LDs were also reduced and this significantly impaired cancer radioresistance.
source: When the levels of the main protein responsible for iron storage decreased, LDs were also reduced and this significantly impaired cancer RR.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that FTH1 silencing reduced LDs and increased radiosensitivity.

claim: FTH1 role is crucial for iron storage within the cell and maintenance of redox homeostasis.
source: As well known, the FTH1 role is crucial for the iron storage within the cell and the maintenance of the redox homeostasis.
evidence: The claim represents established scientific knowledge about FTH1 function.

claim: When FTH1 expression is downregulated, the balance between iron uptake and release is compromised.
source: When its expression is downregulated, the balance between the iron uptake and release is compromised.
evidence: The claim is inferred from established knowledge about FTH1 function and supported by the experimental data showing changes in TfR1 and FPN expression.

claim: When FTH1 expression is downregulated, the free cellular iron amount becomes critical for correct cellular functions.
source: By consequence, the free cellular iron amount becomes critical for the correct cellular functions (Wang et al., 2010; Rouault, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2010 and Rouault, 2006, indicating established scientific knowledge.

claim: Iron imbalance plays a central role in LD accumulation.
source: Here we found that this iron imbalance assumed also a central role in the LD accumulation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that manipulating iron homeostasis affects LD content.

claim: FTH1 overexpression fully restored the LD pool in both H460 and MCF7 FTH1-silenced cell lines.
source: Moreover, such an overexpression fully restored the LD pool (Figure 4C–D) in both cell lines
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: FTH1 overexpression in FTH1-silenced cells resulted in cells reacquiring higher radioresistance.
source: which also reacquired a higher RR (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by clonogenic assay data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Deferoxamine (DFO) is a high-affinity Fe3+ chelator and an FDA approved drug used to treat patients with iron overload.
source: DFO is a high-affinity Fe3+ chelator and an FDA approved drug used to treat patients with iron overload.
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about DFO as an FDA-approved drug.

claim: Iron chelation by DFO was able to induce LD accumulation in FTH1-silenced H460 and MCF7 cells.
source: LD540 staining on both treated H460shFTH1 (H460 shFTH1+ DFO) and MCF7 shFTH1 (MCF7 shFTH1+ DFO) univocally showed that the iron chelation was able to induce LD accumulation (Figure 4F–G)
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claim: DFO-induced LD accumulation in FTH1-silenced cells conferred higher survival ability to cells after radiation treatment.
source: and this, in turn, conferred higher survival ability to cells after radiation treatment, as shown by clonogenic assays (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by clonogenic assay data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Radiotherapy has greatly improved from both a technical and a bio-clinical point of view since its first application in cancer treatment.
source: Since its first application in cancer treatment, radiotherapy has greatly improved from both a technical and a bio-clinical point of view, significantly increasing the treatment options and patient survival.
evidence: The claim represents general knowledge about the historical development of radiotherapy.

claim: Ionizing radiations (X-rays) work by damaging cell biomolecules, mostly DNA, which eventually induce cell death.
source: Ionizing radiations (X-rays) work by damaging cell biomolecules, mostly DNA, which eventually induce cell death.
evidence: The claim represents established scientific knowledge about the mechanism of action of ionizing radiation.

claim: Cancer cell radioresistance makes different tumor types difficult to treat.
source: Cancer cell radioresistance (RR) makes different tumor types difficult to treat.
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about clinical challenges in radiotherapy.

claim: The presence within the tumor mass of cancer stem cells (CSCs) or cancer-initiating cells (CICs) represents one of the driving forces contributing to tumor resistance and recurrence after radiotherapy treatments.
source: In this regard, the presence within the tumor mass of a small cell subpopulation called cancer stem cells (CSCs) or cancer-initiating cells (CICs) seems to represent one of the driving forces contributing to tumor resistance and recurrence after radiotherapy treatments (Baumann et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Baumann et al., 2008, indicating established scientific knowledge.

claim: Lipid metabolic reprogramming in cancer cells has become a central aspect of cancer aggressiveness.

claim: An increase of lipid droplets inside cancer cells has been shown to correlate with a CSC phenotype in colon, ovary, breast, and glioblastoma cancers.
source: In particular, an increase of small lipid organelles inside cancer cells, namely lipid droplets (LDs), has been shown to correlate with a CSC phenotype in colon (Tirinato, 2015) ovary (Li, 2017), breast (Havas, 2017), and glioblastoma (Kant et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies (Tirinato, 2015; Li, 2017; Havas, 2017; Kant et al., 2020).

source: Cell survival upon radiation treatment is also modulated by several tumor parameters such as hypoxia, oxidative stress, inflammation, acidic stress, and low glucose, all of which have been reported to mediate their effects through iron metabolism (Schonberg, 2015).

claim: Free radicals are considered strong contributors to tumor proliferation and aggressiveness.

source: Ferritin is a protein complex composed of two chains, light (FTL) and heavy (FTH)
evidence: The claim represents established scientific knowledge about ferritin structure.

claim: Ferritin's clinical importance has been demonstrated in many cancers through multiple roles: contribution to tumorigenesis, restoration of tumor-dependent vessel growth, and association with tissue invasion.
source: and its clinical importance has been demonstrated in many cancers through multiple roles: the contribution to tumorigenesis, the restoration of tumor-dependent vessel growth, and the association with tissue invasion (Schonberg, 2015; Aversa et al., 2017).

claim: High levels of ferritin are often found in patients with various advanced cancers, which could potentially be treated with radiotherapy.

source: The subpopulation containing the highest amount of LDs (LDHigh) showed a higher clonogenic potential compared to the LDLow counterpart.

claim: These data provide evidence of a new pivotal role for LDs in cancer radioresistance linking their expression with iron metabolism and specifically to FTH1 expression.

source: Increased LD amount has been found in various cancer cells with stem-like properties, including colorectal cancer cells (Tirinato, 2015), glioblastoma cells (Kant et al., 2020), and breast cancer cells (Havas, 2017).

claim: Radiation exposure might enrich the heterogeneous population with cells having a stemness-like phenotype.
source: Although we did not screen all the putative stemness markers, our preliminary data indicates that radiation exposure might enrich the heterogeneous population with cells having a stemness-like phenotype, which is in agreement with previous works (Ghisolfi et al., 2012; Woodward et al., 2007).

claim: High ROS levels are commonly found in many cancer cells.
source: Indeed, high ROS levels are commonly found in many cancer cells

claim: The presence of a higher LD amount is an intrinsic feature of cells and may represent a selective advantage which might allow resistant cells to survive damages induced by ROS production following exposure to ionizing radiation.
source: This indicates that the presence of a higher LD amount was an intrinsic feature of the cells and may represent a selective advantage which might allow resistant cells to survive damages, induced by ROS production following exposure to ionizing radiation.

claim: Ferritin has been shown to be elevated in some tumor tissues, suggesting that increased iron storage in cancer cells might contribute to cell survival.
source: However, in cancer cells, iron homeostasis is dysregulated, and Ferritin, the protein involved in iron storage, has been shown to be elevated in some tumor tissues, thus suggesting that increased iron storage in cancer cells might contribute to cell survival (Bystrom et al., 2014).

claim: Studies on Ferritin and iron roles in radiotherapy are limited.

claim: Naz and colleagues demonstrated an upregulation of hepatic ferritin and elevated FTL serum levels in sham-irradiated rats.
source: Naz and colleagues demonstrated an upregulation of hepatic ferritin and elevated FTL serum levels in sham-irradiated rats (Wang et al., 2010).

claim: Cells with reduced ability to store iron showed reduced radioresistance.

claim: In the absence of adequate levels of FTH1, treatment with an iron chelator was able to reduce the iron excess inside cells, causing significant LD re-accumulation in FTH1-silenced cell lines.

claim: Iron homeostasis is strongly correlated with the surviving ability of radioresistant cells.
source: Therefore, iron homeostasis is strongly correlated with the surviving ability of the RR cells
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental results showing that manipulating iron homeostasis affects radioresistance.

claim: LDs are important mediators in the processes linking iron homeostasis to radioresistance.
source: and LDs are important mediators in these processes.

claim: The FTH1-LD interconnection was seen in mice ablated for both iron regulatory proteins 1 and 2 (IRP1 and IRP2) using Cre/Lox technology.
source: Notably, the FTH1-LD interconnection was also seen in mice ablated for both iron regulatory proteins 1 and 2 (IRP1 and IRP2) using Cre/Lox technology (Galy et al., 2008; Galy, 2010).

claim: Understanding the mechanisms behind radiation responses may suggest novel strategies for increasing radiotherapy curative capacity.

claim: Cells containing the highest LDs showed the highest clonogenic potential after irradiation.
